close_reason: Closed as workspace-API observation deferred to JMAP-glx8.4 (aligned to the 3-sibling consensus camp). The opposite-direction propagation (align all 4 extension-types siblings to EmailComparator's skip_serializing_if + bool_true pattern) is filed as JMAP-18qe — a workspace-API sweep, not a per-crate fix. Local contacts-types behavior matches Tasks/Calendars siblings.
description:
EmailComparator (jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:310-311) declares:
    #[serde(default = "bool_true", skip_serializing_if = "is_true")]
    pub is_ascending: bool,

Result on the wire: is_ascending is omitted when ascending (the default), present only when descending. Smaller wire footprint, matches the JMAP spec convention that defaults are omittable.

ContactCardComparator (card.rs:332-333) and the calendars/tasks siblings declare:
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub is_ascending: bool,

Result: always emitted, even when ascending.

Wire-format spec-conformant in both cases. Worth noting because EmailComparator is the canonical-template authority for the extension-types family, and this is a real wire-format divergence. Either propagate skip_serializing_if to the sibling comparators (smaller wire output, matches mail-types) or document why the simpler 'always-emit' shape is right here. The 4-sibling consensus (calendars, tasks×2, contacts) is the simpler 'always-emit' shape, so adding skip_serializing_if would be the propagation direction; bd JMAP-glx8.4 covers the broader divergence.

Do NOT fix in isolation — file as a workspace-API observation tied to the canonical-template propagation decision. The four siblings should resolve together.
title: ContactCardComparator is_ascending wire format differs from EmailComparator default-skip
